title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
summary: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.

title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
summary: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},μ_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.

title: The taming of 3-fold flops
comment: contribution to Proceeding of the ICM 2026
summary: This article overviews recent progress in understanding and classifying one of the most elementary of birational surgeries within algebraic geometry, namely 3-fold flops, through the development of a noncommutative version of singularity theory.

title: The classification of smooth 3-fold flops
summary: This paper establishes the analytic classification of smooth, simple, 3-fold flops, and in the process provides both an intrinsic characterisation and a classification of their contraction algebras.

title: Exact Archimedean Flicker--Rallis Periods on Cohomological Minimal $K$-Types
summary: For the symmetric pair $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C),\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb R))$, we compute the exact Flicker--Rallis period of a distinguished vector in a cohomological minimal $U(n)$-type, normalized by the Gel'fand--Tsetlin pairing of Hara--Miyazaki--Namikawa. Our main tool is a weight-independent identity between the Whittaker period and a compact $O(n)$-average. We determine the proportionality constant using the archimedean newform formula of Humphries--Jo, and evaluate the compact functional on the normalized distinguished vector. This yields an explicit formula for the Flicker--Rallis period for every cohomological weight.

title: Weyl chambers, asymptotic expansions, and blowup analysis of explicit Toda solutions
summary: Blowup analysis is a central part of geometric analysis, and systems of PDEs such as Toda systems exhibit particularly rich blowup behavior. In [Nie25], the author constructed explicit families of radial Toda solutions whose blowup masses correspond to arbitrary elements of the Weyl group of the underlying Lie algebra. In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. The key is an asymptotic analysis of the solution family that distinguishes Cartan elements in the interior of a Weyl chamber from those lying on its boundary faces. We prove a uniform upper bound for $u_i^{λ,H}(r)+2\log r$, so that the selection estimate holds with the center at the origin. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_μ$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.

title: Rigid and $τ$-locally free modules via Taft algebras
summary: We show that rigid modules are $τ$-locally free for a large family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras. This family includes many cases of the algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schröer in their Inventiones paper "Quivers with relations for symmetrizable Cartan matrices I: Foundations", hence answering a question posed by Geiss--Leclerc--Schröer for many new cases. Our result is achieved by introducing coactions of Taft algebras and applying the recent theory developed by the first-named author and Coulembier.

title: Drinfeld presentation of affine iquantum groups via iHopf algebras
summary: Affine quantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ and affine iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors $Θ_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ explicitly in terms of the root vectors $ψ^\pm_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, thereby extending the results of Li and Przeździecki for certain affine types of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$.

title: $\SL_3$ dual pairs
summary: We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.

title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
summary: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
summary: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided.

title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
comment: 19 pages; v2: a discussion of quantization of Fourier matrices added
summary: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two complementary Lagrangian subalgebras.

title: Segre determinants and MHV gravity amplitudes
summary: We describe a Segre-Veronese construction of polynomial solutions to the interpolation conditions of the numerators of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes given by Hodges' formula. The five- and six-point Hodges numerators arise from Segre determinants, while for every $n\geq7$ suitable Segre determinants lead to solutions linearly independent of the Hodges numerator. The existence of such independent elements for $n=7,8$ was recently established by Mai and Zhang.

title: Unipotent representations and the categorical trace of Frobenius
summary: We give a new proof of the classification of unipotent representations for split finite groups of Lie type. To do this, we first construct an (infinity, 2)-categorification of Lusztig's map from the Hecke algebra to the asymptotic algebra. Then we use the theory of weights to show that it induces an isomorphism after applying trace of Frobenius.

title: Regulator Constants and Cohomology
comment: 24 pages - some typos have been corrected and some sentences have been reformulated
summary: We show how regulator constants of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module can be related to $G$-cohomology, where $G$ is a finite group. We then derive consequences of such relation for modules naturally arising in number theory, such as ring of integers and units of number fields, $K$-theory groups of ring of integers and Mordell-Weil groups of elliptic curves.

title: Representations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and hyperplane complements
comment: v2: Referee comments incorporated. To appear in J. Lond. Math. Soc. v1: Comments are more than welcomed!
summary: We study faithful realisations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and study Vinberg systems associated to them. We show that they induce embeddings of hyperplane complements, which provide geometrical realisations of certain types of strong admissible (LCM) homomorphisms between Artin--Tits groups.

title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
comment: 127p, v2: Sections C.2.12, C.3.45-C.3.50 are added. Lemma C.3.38 is improved, some typos corrected
summary: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

title: The Schützenberger involution and colored lattice models
summary:
Colored lattice models can be used to describe many different types of special functions of interest in both algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, for example Schur polynomials, nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, and characters and Whittaker functions for representations of p-adic groups. A notable example is the metaplectic ice model of which there are actually two different variants: a Gamma and a Delta variant. These variants differ in key aspects but surprisingly produce equal partition functions, which are weighted sums over admissible configurations, and this equality is called the Gamma-Delta duality. The duality was used to prove the analytic continuation of certain multiple Dirichlet series and is highly non-trivial, especially since the number of configurations on each side of the equality can differ.
  In this paper we generalize the Gamma-Delta duality by constructing a new family of solvable, colored lattice models and prove that they are dual to existing lattice models in the literature. Besides the above metaplectic case we also get a new lattice model and Gamma-Delta type duality for (non-metaplectic) Iwahori Whittaker functions together with a crystal limit for Demazure atoms for Cartan type A. The equality of partition functions is shown using Yang-Baxter equations involving both variants of lattice models simultaneously.
  For the crystal lattice model we show that the duality refines to a weight-respecting bijection of states given by the Schützenberger involution on the associated Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns or semistandard Young tableaux. We also show how the individual steps exchanging two rows in the proof of the duality for the partition functions refines to Berenstein-Kirillov or, equivalently, Bender-Knuth involutions.

title: Counting stringy points on a family of character varieties
summary: We provide explicit formulas for the number of stringy points over finite fields of parabolic type A character varieties with generic semisimple monodromy. This leads to formulas for their stringy E-polynomials. In particular, they satisfy the Betti Topological Mirror Symmetry Conjecture of T. Hausel and M. Thaddeus and a refinement regarding isotypic components. Our proof is based on a Frobenius-type formula for Clifford-type settings and an analysis of it in a specific set-up related to regular wreath products with cyclic groups.

title: Quantum theory of molecular orientation
comment: 12 + 38 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables, 50 examples; v5 minor corrections
summary: We formulate a quantum phase space for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules. For each nuclear spin isomer, we re-derive the isomer's admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data, introduce its angular position states using quantization theory, and develop a generalized Fourier transform converting between the two. We classify molecules into three types -- asymmetric, rotationally symmetric, and perrotationally symmetric -- with the last type having no macroscopic analogue due to nuclear-spin statistics constraints. We discuss two general features in perrotationally symmetric state spaces that are Hamiltonian-independent and induced solely by symmetry and spin statistics. First, we quantify when and how an isomer's state space is completely rotation-spin entangled, meaning that it does not admit any separable states. Second, we identify isomers whose position states house an internal pseudo-spin or "fiber" degree of freedom, and the fiber's Berry phase or matrix after adiabatic changes in position yields naturally robust operations, akin to braiding anyonic quasiparticles or realizing fault-tolerant quantum gates. We outline how the fiber can be used as a quantum error-correcting code and discuss scenarios where these features can be experimentally probed

title: Cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type
comment: 45 pages, 2 figures. Version 2: Fixed typographical error. Version 3: Fixed an error in the proof of a main result, corrected typos, other minor changes. Version 4: Corrected typos, other minor changes. We thank an anonymous referee for many helpful comments. Version 5: Final pre-publication version, to appear in Comptes Rendus
summary: We give an explicit construction of the cluster scattering diagram for any acyclic exchange matrix of affine type. We show that the corresponding cluster scattering fan coincides both with the mutation fan and with a fan constructed in the almost-positive roots model.

title: On invariant $1$-dimensional representations of a finite $W$-algebra
comment: Journal version of the paper. Compared to v1, the paper was significantly revised and rewritten. Theorem 1.2 was added as the second main result of the paper, and Section 6 was added, proving this theorem
summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra over $\mathbf{C}$ and $G$ be the corresponding simply connected algebraic group. Consider a nilpotent element $e\in \mathfrak{g}$, the corresponding element $χ=(e, \bullet)$ in $\mathfrak{g}^*$, and the coadjoint orbit $\mathbf{O}=Gχ$. We are interested in the set $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ of codimension $1$ ideals $J\subset \mathcal{W}$ in a finite $W$-algebra $\mathcal{W}=U(\mathfrak{g}, e)$. We have a natural action of the component group $Γ=Z_G(χ)/Z_G^\circ(χ)$ on $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$. Denote the set of $Γ$-stable points of $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ by $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^Γ$. For a classical $\mathfrak{g}$ Premet and Topley proved that $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^Γ$ are parameterized by the points of an affine space. In this paper we will give an alternative proof of this fact using completely different approach. As a corollary of our construction, we imply that for classical $\mathfrak{g}$ all $Γ$-invariant $1$-dimensional representations of $\mathcal{W}$ are obtained by a parabolic induction introduced by Losev.
